title: A Cosmic Cobweb
caption: The galaxy cluster Abell 611, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
credit: ESA/Hubble, NASA, P. Kelly, M. Postman, J. Richard, S. Allen

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Hundreds of small galaxies scatter across this view, some in shades of orange and others white. Most are fuzzy ovals, though a few show clear spiral arms. Many thin, long orange arcs curve around the centre of the image, where a strong orange glow sits. This is the galaxy cluster Abell 611, in the constellation Lynx.
Hubble released this inky image in celebration of Halloween, and the web of galaxies does have a cobweb feel. But the cluster is also a serious scientific target.

Those curved arcs are examples of strong gravitational lensing. The cluster's mass bends light from galaxies far behind it, stretching them into arcs around its centre. Because the amount of bending depends on how much mass the cluster contains, including dark matter that gives off no light, lensed arcs like these make Abell 611 a popular place to investigate dark matter.
scale: The cluster lies roughly 3.2 billion light-years from Earth, according to ESA/Hubble.

understand.summary: This image combines Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys and Wide Field Camera 3, with many filters from visible light into the near-infrared. The packet does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.
filters: 850 nm · Optical Long pass z (Hubble ACS)
understand.eye: Much of this data is near-infrared light, invisible to the eye, and the faint lensed arcs need Hubble's exposures to appear.
